query: Using the reported HfZrTiTa0.53 refractory high-entropy alloy as the starting material and its quasi-static properties—786 MPa yield strength, 1314 MPa compressive strength, and 13.5% fracture strain—as the baseline, what single testable hypothesis proposes an intervention to overcome limited strain hardening, poor uniform deformability, and rapid failure as strain rate increases under adiabatic dynamic deformation? Specify the intervention and mechanism, predict changes relative to the baseline in strength, uniform deformation, localization resistance, and impact-induced energy release, define the strain-rate and loading conditions over which the prediction applies, cite supporting evidence from the reported refractory-alloy literature, and describe a matched baseline-versus-intervention experiment that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The HfZrTiTa0.53 refractory high-entropy alloy will exhibit improved strain hardening, uniform deformability, and resistance to rapid failure under adiabatic dynamic deformation when subjected to a grain refinement intervention, resulting in enhanced strength, ductility, and localization resistance.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast HfZrTiTa0.53 refractory high-entropy alloy with a yield strength of 786 MPa, compressive strength of 1314 MPa, and fracture strain of 13.5%
generation.intervention: Grain refinement through severe plastic deformation or other methods to reduce grain size and increase grain boundary density
generation.conditions: Adiabatic dynamic deformation at strain rates ranging from 1000 s−1 to 3000 s−1
generation.mechanism: Grain refinement leads to increased grain boundary density, which enhances strain hardening and improves uniform deformability by reducing the formation of adiabatic shear bands
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved strength, ductility, and localization resistance under adiabatic dynamic deformation, with a predicted increase in yield strength of at least 10% and a decrease in fracture strain of at least 20%
generation.baseline: As-cast HfZrTiTa0.53 refractory high-entropy alloy with a yield strength of 786 MPa, compressive strength of 1314 MPa, and fracture strain of 13.5%
generation.boundary: Strain rates ranging from 1000 s−1 to 3000 s−1
generation.uncertainty: The exact magnitude of the improvement in strength, ductility, and localization resistance is uncertain and requires further experimentation to quantify

falsification_experiment.design: Quasi-static and dynamic compression tests on as-cast and grain-refined HfZrTiTa0.53 refractory high-entropy alloy samples
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the grain-refined samples do not exhibit improved strength, ductility, and localization resistance under adiabatic dynamic deformation compared to the as-cast samples, the hypothesis is falsified

AbstractThis paper investigates the effect of strain rate on the mechanical deformation and microstructural development of dual-phase AlCrFe2Ni2 high-entropy alloy during quasi-static and dynamic compression processes. It is revealed that the as-cast AlCrFe2Ni2 alloy is composed of a mixture of FCC, disordered BCC, and ordered B2 crystal structure phases. The alloy shows excellent compressive properties under quasi-static and dynamic deformation. The yield strength exceeds 600 MPa while the compressive strength is more than 3000 MPa at the compression rates of 30% under quasi-static conditions. Under dynamic compression conditions, the ultimate compression stresses are 1522 MPa, 1816 MPa, and 1925 MPa with compression strains about 12.8%, 14.7%, and 18.2% at strain rates of 1300 s−1, 1700 s−1 and 2100 s−1, respectively. The dynamic yield strength is approximately linear with strain rate within the specified range and exhibit great sensitivity. In this work, the effect of strain rate on the microstructural evolution and compression behavior of the dual-phase AlCrFe2Ni2 alloy was studied. The main conclusions are as follows: The as-cast AlCrFe2Ni2 alloy is composed of a mixture of Fe,Ni-enriched FCC phases, disordered Fe,Cr-enriched BCC phases, and ordered Al,Ni-enriched B2 phases. The AlCrFe2Ni2 alloy shows excellent compressive properties under quasi-static deformation. The yield strength exceeds 600 MPa while the compressive strength is more than 3000 MPa at the compression rates of 30%. The ultimate compression stresses are 1522 MPa, 1816 MPa, and 1925 MPa with compression strains about 12.8%, 14.7%, and 18.2% at strain rates of 1300 s−1, 1700 s−1, and 2100 s−1, respectively. Strain rate sensitivity ranges from 0.0089 at low strain (10−4 s−1–100 s−1) to 0.42 at high strain rates (1300 s−1–2100 s−1), which is due to the phonon drag effect at high strains. At high-strain-rate compression, a adiabatic shear phenomenon occurs. The adiabatic shear bands formed by dynamic recrystallization due to the conflicting processes of strain rate hardening and heat softening.

As expected, the strength of this alloy increases with strain rate (10−3 s−1 < 1.7 × 103 s−1 < 6 × 105 s−1), as shown earlier for a similar HEA (). The quasi-static and dynamic stress-strain curves both illustrate the high strength of this alloy between 1 and 2 GPa. This, however, does not markedly compromise the ductility as, under quasi-static deformation, the alloy continues to exhibit work hardening up to a strain of 0.8, despite the fact that it had already been predeformed by swaging, to result in a final total strain of 0.95. This dual strength and ductility response serve to ensure a high toughness, even under extreme loading conditions. In the dynamic shear experiment, the equivalent strain is actually much higher, reaching a value of 1.5. Beyond this point, there is a drop of flow stress caused by the local temperature rise due to severe localization, a phenomenon known as adiabatic shear localization, as described in the Supplementary Materials.
